consensus_summary: Consensus identifies garden primarily as paradise (Eden): the place of God's presence, unbroken fellowship, divine provision and life, framing the arc from creation through redemption to new-creation restoration, with complementary alternatives (temple/sanctuary, bride/soul, watered/fruitful life, Gethsemane obedience).
book_summary: Garden is a planted stand of trees that constitutes a grouping of nations.
consensus_core_identification: paradise/Eden as the locus of divine presence and fellowship (lost and restored)
book_core_identification: planted stand of trees = grouping of nations
boundary_disagreement: Consensus centers every major garden (Eden, Song, Gethsemane, tomb, New Jerusalem) inside the paradise/fellowship category; the book relocates the term entirely to a national collective via tree imagery and thereby excludes the paradise core.
material_contradiction: The two cores cannot both be the primary identification of the same biblical symbol: accepting 'grouping of nations' requires discarding paradise/divine-fellowship as the central referent.
rationale: Minimum cores are paradise (consensus) versus nations-group (book). The latter is not a narrowing, broadening or re-boundary of the former; it replaces the referent. No consensus primary or listed alternative anticipates the nations reading drawn from Ezek 31, so the identifications stand in material contradiction rather than refinement or mere novelty.
strongest_objection: The single Ezek 31:9 citation (and its trees cross-reference) cannot override the pervasive Eden-to-New-Jerusalem paradise motif that dominates the rest of Scripture and all mainstream traditions.
